manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the phone on the box and place it on the phone stand to the right.

Task description: Move the phone with a white frame and dark screen, lying on the white box, to the light-colored phone stand on its right so the stand supports it stably.

Success criteria: The phone is on the phone stand to the right and remains stably in place after the gripper opens, without slipping or tipping.

## Execution tips

- Consider gripping the middle of both long phone edges, avoiding side buttons and leaving the lower end free to seat in the stand hooks. Open slightly wider than the phone and watch the pens on both sides.
- The phone is close to the box surface. Approach with pads contacting its side frame rather than fingertips pressing the box or pushing the phone away. Confirm the fingers actually straddle it before closing rather than merely overlapping in view.
- If adjusting the phone's tilt, make small changes where it is clear of the box and has room around it. Watch the swing of both ends to avoid the stand or tabletop objects.
- Place the phone back toward the stand's inclined panel and lower its bottom into the supporting hooks, avoiding forward pressure on the stand. Release gradually once securely supported, and watch for fingertips catching the phone or hooks during withdrawal.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start the single authorized real-robot episode with the specified parameters and act on the returned manual and live observations.

I have read the manual and confirmed that only the right arm is available. The phone remains flat on the box surface. I am adjusting the gripper pose at a raised height, then will approach both sides in small steps and check the grasp.

One pose adjustment reached a controller joint limit, and recovery was allowed. I have adjusted the approach path based on the new measured pose; the phone and nearby objects do not appear to have moved.

The gripper is nearly aligned with the phone's two long edges. Next I will lower by no more than 1 cm at a time, confirm the pads reach the side edges before closing, and make a short test lift first.
The gripper-close command has been issued. I am waiting for its actual opening to stabilize, then will check whether the phone is grasped.
The test lift showed the phone remains on the box surface and is not securely grasped. I reopened the gripper and will correct the height before grasping again.

After correction, the actual gripper opening stopped near 75 mm, and the phone lifted and tilted during the test lift. I will continue raising in small steps and confirm the entire phone clears the box without sliding before lateral transfer.

The phone remains between the grippers, but its angle keeps changing during lifting, and it is unclear whether the far end has fully cleared the box surface. I will continue lifting in small steps and check; I will not move it laterally yet.

At the current grasp point, one end of the phone remains pressed against the box surface, making the pose unstable. I will lower it slowly back onto the box, then move the grasp point closer to the middle.
The phone is back on the box surface, and the gripper moved about 3 cm along its long side toward the middle. I am realigning to the side edge height, then will test-lift again.
After this test lift, the phone remained in the gripper and is now nearly vertical. I am increasing clearance from the box surface while adjusting the wrist angle to avoid the joint limit.
The phone slipped back onto the box during wrist adjustment and remains there rather than on the stand. I will realign to its new position, adopt a more vertical grasp and check edge-grasp depth.

I have aligned with the phone's new position using a more vertical gripper, with the grasp point between the previous two. Next I will descend in smaller increments to confirm edge contact and check whether it lifts smoothly.

The phone maintained its relative position to the gripper during lifting and slight rotation, indicating a more reliable grasp. Next I will move gradually toward the right stand and reduce step size near the hooks.

The phone has been moved to the front left of the phone stand, and the grasp remains stable. I am aligning the back of the phone with the stand backboard, then will adjust the bottom edge and support hooks in small steps.

The controller reported that authorization cannot cover the next action and returned `done=true`. I will end this episode and send no further motion commands. The gripper still holds the phone in front of the stand; stable support by the phone stand has not been confirmed, and the on-site operator must take over.
